organization.name: CareSource
organization.short_description: CareSource is a nonprofit, managed care organization serving over 2.4 million members in Medicaid, Marketplace, and Medicare programs across multiple states. Headquartered in Dayton, Ohio, CareSource is one of the largest Medicaid managed care plans in the country.

contactAnalysis.name: Rick Van Hoose
contactAnalysis.title: Chief Information Officer
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: CIO with direct authority over technology investment decisions and IT strategy.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Present business case after pilot results. Focus on clear ROI tied to state expansion and member retention during Medicaid unwinding.

contactAnalysis.name: Amanda Dix
contactAnalysis.title: VP, Data & Analytics
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Owns data strategy and analytics — ideal champion for AI/ML initiatives that enhance their data capabilities.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: First touch target. Lead with SDoH analytics use case — how AI can improve care coordination for highest-cost Medicaid members.

contactAnalysis.name: James Wilson
contactAnalysis.title: Director, Innovation & Digital Health
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Innovation leader actively seeking new technologies — natural internal advocate for AI solutions.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Second entry point. Frame around digital-first member experience and how AI scales personalization across new state markets.

contactAnalysis.name: Sarah Kumar
contactAnalysis.title: Director, Enterprise Architecture
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Technical architect who will assess platform integration, security, and scalability requirements.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Provide detailed Azure and Databricks integration documentation. She needs to see clean technical fit with existing infrastructure.

contactAnalysis.name: Patricia Moore
contactAnalysis.title: Chief Medical Officer
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: CMO will evaluate clinical AI applications and ensure alignment with quality and outcomes goals.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Build clinical credibility with outcomes data and HEDIS score improvement evidence from similar Medicaid plans.

contactAnalysis.name: Thomas Reed
contactAnalysis.title: VP, Compliance & Regulatory Affairs
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Compliance VP will scrutinize AI for regulatory risk, especially in Medicaid — must be engaged early.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Proactively share Medicaid-specific compliance documentation. Address state-by-state regulatory variation for AI in care management.

signals.aiStrategy: CareSource is investing in predictive analytics for social determinants of health (SDoH) interventions and has launched an AI-powered care coordination platform for complex Medicaid populations. They are exploring generative AI for member communication and health literacy, and building ML models for claims fraud detection.

plan.executiveSummary: CareSource is a high-value mid-market target that combines meaningful scale ($14B, 2.4M members) with the agility to adopt new technology faster than larger competitors. Their SDoH analytics investment, digital-first member experience, and cloud migration signal readiness for AI adoption. The nonprofit mission creates a values-aligned selling opportunity — frame AI as a tool to better serve vulnerable Medicaid populations. State expansion creates immediate need for scalable technology.
plan.painToProductFit:
1. SDoH DATA INTEGRATION: Medicaid populations have complex social needs — AI can synthesize SDoH data from multiple sources to create actionable intervention recommendations.
2. MEMBER COMMUNICATION: Lower health literacy and diverse language needs in Medicaid populations — AI-powered personalized communication improves engagement.
3. CARE COORDINATION: Complex Medicaid populations require intelligent automation to prioritize outreach, predict care gaps, and optimize case manager workflows.
4. STATE EXPANSION: Each new state brings new regulatory requirements, provider networks, and demographics — AI accelerates market entry.
plan.competitiveThreats: DATABRICKS: Already embedded as analytics platform — may upsell AI/ML capabilities. INOVALON: Strong healthcare analytics with Medicaid expertise. NAVU HEALTH: Focused on Medicaid population health with AI. INTERNAL BUILD: Growing data science team may prefer building on existing Databricks platform. CONSULTING: Deloitte and PwC have Medicaid-focused practices competing for this work.
plan.timingUrgency: Active state expansion means technology decisions being made NOW for new market infrastructure. Medicaid redetermination requires sophisticated member outreach to retain eligible members. Cloud migration to Azure creates natural window for cloud-native AI. Larger competitors (Centene, Molina) investing heavily in AI — CareSource must keep pace.
plan.dealStrategy: Mission-aligned mid-market sale over 2-4 months. Phase 1: Connect through Amanda Dix (VP Data & Analytics) with SDoH use case. Phase 2: Complimentary SDoH assessment showing AI impact on highest-cost members. Phase 3: Clinical credibility with CMO Patricia Moore using outcomes data. Phase 4: Business case to CIO Rick Van Hoose tied to state expansion ROI. Phase 5: Pilot in Ohio Medicaid market. Estimated deal size: $200K-500K initial, $2M+ enterprise. Risks: nonprofit price sensitivity, Databricks incumbency.
plan.discoveryQuestions:
1. How are you currently identifying and addressing social determinants of health for your Medicaid members?
2. What's your biggest technology challenge as you expand into new state markets?
3. How do you measure the effectiveness of your care coordination programs today?
4. What percentage of member outreach actually reaches the intended recipient and drives action?
5. Where are you in your cloud migration journey, and what workloads are you prioritizing?
plan.roiFramework: Care coordination automation: Reduce case manager caseload by 30% = $8-12M annually in labor costs. Claims accuracy: 2% improvement on $14B portfolio = $280M in reduced rework. Member retention: AI outreach during redetermination retaining additional 5% = ~$700M retained revenue. SDoH interventions: 10% reduction in ER utilization for targeted members. PILOT: 60-day pilot focused on SDoH-powered care coordination in Ohio Medicaid, target 20% improvement in engagement rates.
